title: Styles
description: Practise the 14 Advanced Higher Styles concepts from the Music Dictionary.

items.prompt: An English sacred choral work with a religious text, first used in Renaissance Protestant worship.
The course term for a simple song or melody, including a late-Renaissance English solo song with lute accompaniment.
A light, dance-like English madrigal with a recurring fa-la-la refrain.
A German Lutheran hymn tune, usually in a clear regular rhythm.
Recent jazz using improvisation with extended or chromatic harmony, complex rhythms, electronics or unusual instrumental techniques.
Dance music made mainly with electronic instruments and computers, often for clubs.
A lively Renaissance court dance in triple metre, often following a slower pavan.
A secular Renaissance vocal work, usually for several unaccompanied voices.
A sacred Renaissance choral work, usually polyphonic and in Latin, using a text outside the fixed Mass movements.
Art music that deliberately draws on the folk culture or identity of a nation.
Name the 20th-century revival of earlier forms and Classical balance using modern harmony and rhythm, associated with works such as Stravinsky’s Pulcinella.
A slow, stately Renaissance court dance, usually in duple metre.
The European historical musical period approximately 1400–1600. Name the period, rather than one of its individual vocal or dance forms.
Name the compositional approach using a predetermined ordered series, especially a row of twelve chromatic pitch classes and its transformations.
